comment: A conversation as a row of steps and what it has become after them (D-294, D-304, D-305). A step is a line of Claude Code, or something the person does. The answer is the state, the feed and every line written to Claude Code on the way. A message sent during a turn, or while a card waits, goes to Claude Code at once and stays grey until Claude Code says it back (--replay-user-messages): then it was taken into the turn (D-341). While a grey message waits, the session stays at work. A turn that ended does not free the session while a subagent still runs. What a subagent says inside its own work stays out of the feed; its requests do not. glance is the conversation as the list of sessions sees it: what it does and the parts of the one line about it. A command of "!" that runs keeps the session at work; a message sent meanwhile waits and goes to Claude with its output, and Esc stops the command without a word to Claude. When Claude Code dies, the grey messages it was given stop waiting.
